successCriteria.description: The Employee entity extends BaseEntity (from shared/types) and exposes exactly the reconciled-architecture canonical field set — email, fullName, role as a plain string, managerId (string|null), department, employmentStatus ('ACTIVE'|'INACTIVE'|'TERMINATED') — NOT the PLAN.md-prescribed employeeCode/firstName/lastName/isActive/role-union. A reviewer can check the type compiles and matches the employees schema in docs/ARCHITECTURE.md.

The repository interface declares exactly four operations — findById(id), findByEmail(email), findManagerId(employeeId), findHrAdmins() — with the settled signatures, and a concrete repository class implements all four against the pg pool.

findById returns the matching Employee or null when no row exists; findByEmail returns the matching Employee or null; findManagerId returns the employee's manager id or null (no manager / employee absent); findHrAdmins returns all employees whose role is HR_ADMIN (empty array when none). Missing data yields null/empty, never a thrown error.

Row-to-entity mapping converts snake_case DB columns to camelCase entity fields (full_name→fullName, manager_id→managerId, employment_status→employmentStatus, created_at→createdAt, updated_at→updatedAt) and materializes timestamp columns as Date instances.

Unit tests mock the pg pool (shared/db/connection) and assert correct SQL text and bind-parameter usage plus row-to-entity mapping for all four operations, including the null-result and empty-list cases.

The barrel (src/modules/employee/index.ts) exports Employee, IEmployeeRepository, and EmployeeRepository; the module compiles under strict TypeScript (no implicit any, strict null checks) and `npm run build` + `npx jest` pass with the new files.

constraints: All database access goes through the repository layer (GP-001 / no-direct-db-outside-repository). The EmployeeRepository is the only component that touches the pg pool; the model and barrel contain no SQL or pool references.
Use unknown with type guards instead of any (HARNESS no-any rule). Row-to-entity mapping must not rely on `any` casts; the DB row type is treated as unknown/Record<string, unknown> and narrowed.

EmployeeRepository is built directly against the pg.Pool exported from src/shared/db/connection.ts; do not reference src/shared/base.repository.ts (it does not exist on disk despite ARCHITECTURE.md mentioning it).

Modules import from each other ONLY through index.ts barrels; the employee module imports shared/types and shared/db/connection via bare paths (moduleDirectories includes 'src', tsconfig baseUrl is './src'). No relative imports crossing module boundaries.
TypeScript strict mode is enabled — handle managerId: string|null and the employmentStatus union precisely; no implicit any, strict null checks must pass.
No hardcoded secrets (HARNESS no-hardcoded-secrets). The repository must not embed credentials; it consumes the shared pool whose connection string comes from process.env.DATABASE_URL.
outOfScope: EmployeeService and its interface (IEmployeeService) — deferred to Phase 7. This phase produces only the model, repository interface, repository implementation, barrel, and unit tests.
HTTP layer (controller, routes, Fastify plugin) for employee — not part of this phase; no endpoints are defined here.
Write/mutation operations (create, update, delete, status transitions) on employees — only the four read operations (findById, findByEmail, findManagerId, findHrAdmins) are in scope.
Audit logging for employee reads (GP-002 applies to state-changing operations; these are read-only queries and require no audit record).
Database migrations / schema creation for the employees table — schema is assumed to exist per the reconciled architecture; this phase does not generate Knex migrations.

entityInvariants.invariant: employmentStatus is a three-valued lifecycle state ('ACTIVE'|'INACTIVE'|'TERMINATED'); INACTIVE and TERMINATED are distinct (Business Rule 10 blocks leave submission for either), so the entity must NOT collapse them into a single isActive boolean.

managerId is nullable (string|null): an employee may have no manager, which is the trigger for the no-manager escalation path (Phase 9). The repository must preserve null rather than coercing to an empty string.

role is a plain string (not a closed 'EMPLOYEE'|'MANAGER'|'HR_ADMIN' union) per the reconciled architecture, so that 'HR_ADMIN' is queryable by findHrAdmins without an enum constraint; the entity type must not narrow role to a fixed union.
Employee extends BaseEntity from src/shared/types/index.ts, inheriting id, createdAt, updatedAt; it does not redeclare those base fields with conflicting types.

interfaceConstraints.errorSemantics: Returns null when no row matches the id; does not throw on missing data. Throws only on infrastructure/pool failure (unhandled rejection prohibited per GP-006 — errors propagate as rejected promises to the caller).
Returns null when no row matches the email; does not throw on missing data. Throws only on infrastructure/pool failure.
Returns the manager_id of the employee, or null when the employee has no manager or does not exist; does not throw on missing data. Throws only on infrastructure/pool failure.
Returns all employees whose role is 'HR_ADMIN'; returns an empty array when none exist (never null). Throws only on infrastructure/pool failure.

consistencyRequirements.requirement: Employee must extend the BaseEntity interface exactly as exported here (id: string, createdAt: Date, updatedAt: Date) — no redeclaration or drift of the base fields.
The repository must obtain its pg.Pool from this module's exported `pool` (configured from process.env.DATABASE_URL); it must not instantiate its own Pool or read DATABASE_URL directly.

The employees table column set the repository queries must match the conceptual data model here: id, email, full_name, role, manager_id, department, employment_status, created_at, updated_at — with snake_case→camelCase mapping to the entity.

Unit tests must follow the established project test conventions shown here: bare imports via moduleDirectories ('shared/...'), plain describe/it/expect, ts-jest preset, node environment — matching the existing Phase 1 test style.

Test files must match testMatch '**/tests/**/*.test.(ts|js)' and resolve bare module imports via moduleDirectories ['node_modules','src']; the repository test path tests/unit/modules/employee/employee.repository.test.ts must conform to this.

integrationPoints.why: Employee extends BaseEntity; this is the hard Phase 1 dependency — the entity cannot compile without it.
EmployeeRepository executes queries through the shared pool; the repository is the sole DB-access boundary for the employee module (GP-001).

findManagerId and findHrAdmins feed the no-manager escalation flow; findById/findByEmail feed identity and ownership checks. The four-operation interface is the contract these later phases depend on, so signatures must remain stable.

The repository queries the employees table whose columns (full_name, manager_id, department, employment_status) drive row-to-entity mapping; the implementation must align column names with the reconciled schema.
